source.title: On Feature Scaling of Recursive Feature Machines
source.authors: Arunav Gupta; Rohit Mishra; William Luu; Mehdi Bouassami

record.file_problem: Full text is present, with minor OCR/formatting artifacts in equations and dataset-size notation.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a double-descent-like feature-size curve using Recursive Feature Machines and kernel regression rather than deep networks.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-MSE curves as feature size varies, including noise, dataset-size, and target-function variations. Training-iteration details concern validation MSE and do not report test error over epochs, so they are not rows for V2. Dataset size is varied while feature size is scaled proportionally, not compared at fixed feature size near an interpolation threshold, so it is not a V3 test.
record.test_reason: The study reports test-MSE curves for Recursive Feature Machines and a Laplacian kernel as input feature size grows, a new non-deep-network setting. Feature size is grown by appending irrelevant noise columns, which also enlarges the D×D M matrix. Its own results bear on whether a fall-rise-fall risk curve appears outside deep networks (V4). The target-noise sweep also bears on whether the peak depends on label noise (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also state that the late descent past D=0.5N 'appears to be an artifact of the model, not the dataset'. They speculate that adding noise features is analogous to widening a network, via the D×D M-matrix link to first-layer weights. They say more analysis is needed before confirming the double-descent relationship.
record.recipe_differences: Uses feature-size sweeps on synthetic regression data with Recursive Feature Machines and a Laplacian-kernel comparator, rather than scaling deep-network model size.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that the curve shape is unchanged across tested target-noise levels, dataset sizes, and target functions. The Laplacian kernel has different reported inflection points from the RFM.
record.problems: Synthetic regression experiments on RFMs do not test deep networks directly. The study does not identify an interpolation threshold, and most curve values are available only in figures rather than as numerical results in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported scaling outcomes left out. Training-iteration and validation-MSE details were not recorded as rows because the paper does not report test error over training time.

untested.parts: Location of the interpolation threshold. Train MSE is plotted but not described, so the peak (~D=0.5N) is not tied to the point where the training set is fit. Also untested: whether noise-column dimension is a capacity axis comparable to parameter count.
Multiple peaks, the effect of optimally tuned regularization, and how peak height scales with noise. The σ values are small and only shape invariance is reported.
Deep-network width/size scaling. Only RFM and Laplacian kernels are tested.
Sample-size effect at fixed feature size. D is scaled proportionally with N.
Test error over training iterations. Only validation MSE behaviour is mentioned.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting the peak. Peaks scale with D/N, but this is not framed or tested as such a measure.

missing.what: Train MSE curves for RFM and Laplacian versus feature size, needed to locate the interpolation point relative to the test-MSE peak

record.verdict_notes: Short technical report (capstone). All curve evidence is figure-only, so numbers come from the conclusion's verbal summary. The reader's V6 'challenges' was downgraded to limits_scope. The text says only that curve shape is unchanged; V6 allows a variance-driven peak; and the tested σ values are tiny relative to the target scale. Tranche changed from T2 to T3 because this is a new model class and axis rather than a different method on deep networks.

versions.untested_parts: Deep-network model-wise scaling; the tested subjects are RFMs and a Laplacian kernel.
Test error over training epochs or iterations; the iteration detail is about validation MSE.
Increasing sample size at or near a fixed interpolation threshold; feature size is scaled proportionally with dataset size.
The study does not locate a training-set interpolation point or establish that its peak is near that point.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak location across size, epochs, and sample size.
The study varies added target noise but does not test multiple peaks or optimally tuned regularization.
No effective-parameter re-counting or test of whether that produces an ordinary U-shaped curve.
